title: Monocular SLAM: validation against ground truth, then the pool data
subtitle: Gregory German, September 2026. Full report, code and every number: github.com/gregorygerman777-hub/sonar_sim, SLAM/validation/REPORT.md
author: Gregory German
headline: Validation. A keyframe based monocular SLAM (initialisation, map, triangulation, local and global bundle adjustment) was built and checked on data with ground truth. On a rendered scene resembling the pool with exact ground truth it recovers a 10 m trajectory to 0.6 cm (ORB) and 0.2 cm (SIFT), and its 3D map lies within a median 0.9 cm / 0.5 cm of the true surface. On real underwater video (AQUALOC) it is under 1 cm while tracking but loses track, and on the TUM benchmark it is 2 to 4 times less accurate than COLMAP (no loop closure). Ground truth exposed two scale bugs, both fixed with regression tests.

Pool data. The sequential SLAM holds only about 10 consecutive frames. COLMAP registers all 117 frames into one model (0.94 px reprojection error): the camera circles the rock target about twice at constant height, and frames 106 to 117, taken 9.6 minutes later, continue on the same circle. Where both methods pose the same frames, their relative rotations agree to within 1 degree. There is no ground truth, so this is plausible and internally consistent, not verified. The scale is unknown (monocular).

Likely cause of the pool tracking failures. Stills about 2 s apart with moving sunlight caustics. In the synthetic scene, adding moving caustics makes tracking fail at 5 degrees between frames, where the static scene works at 15 degrees.
